title: What is an AI Agent?
description: An introduction to the fundamental concept of an AI Agent and how it differs from traditional software.

sections.content: Definition
An AI Agent is a software entity that perceives its environment through inputs, processes information using a reasoning model, and takes actions to achieve a defined goal.
Key Characteristics
Autonomy: Operates without constant human direction.
Reactivity: Responds to changes in its environment.
Proactivity: Takes initiative to achieve goals.
Social Ability: Interacts with other agents or humans.

title: The Agent Loop: Perceive → Think → Act
description: Explore the core loop that drives every AI agent's behavior.

sections.content: The Core Loop
Every AI agent runs a continuous loop: it perceives its current state, reasons about what to do, and then acts. This cycle repeats until the goal is achieved.
Phase 1: Perceive
The agent receives observations from its environment — this could be text, API responses, sensor data, or any other structured input.
Phase 2: Think
The agent uses an LLM or a rule-based system to reason about the observations and decide the next best action.
Phase 3: Act
The agent executes the chosen action — calling a tool, writing a file, sending a message, or making an API call.

title: Tools & Tool Use in Agents
description: Understanding how agents use tools to interact with the external world.

sections.content: What is a Tool?
A tool is a function or API that an agent can call to perform an action beyond its own reasoning. Tools allow agents to search the web, write code, query databases, and more.
Tool Definition
Tools are defined with a name, description, and a schema for their input parameters. The agent's LLM reads these definitions and decides when and how to call them.
web_search(query: String): Searches the internet.
read_file(path: String): Reads a file from disk.
execute_code(code: String): Runs code in a sandbox.

title: Memory: Short-Term vs Long-Term
description: How AI agents remember information across turns and tasks.

sections.content: Short-Term Memory
Short-term memory is the agent's context window — the conversation history and intermediate results it holds in memory during a single session. It is fast but limited.
Long-Term Memory
Long-term memory is stored externally in a vector database, knowledge base, or traditional database. Agents retrieve relevant memories using semantic search to inform their reasoning.

title: Multi-Agent Systems & Orchestration
description: How multiple specialized agents collaborate to solve complex problems.

sections.content: Why Multi-Agent?

A single agent has limited context and capabilities. Multi-agent systems use a swarm of specialized agents — each an expert in a narrow domain — that work in parallel, dramatically increasing capability and reliability.
Orchestrator vs. Worker
An Orchestrator agent breaks down a complex goal into sub-tasks and delegates them to specialized Worker agents. The Orchestrator then aggregates the results.
Communication Patterns
Sequential: Each agent's output is the next agent's input.
Parallel: Multiple agents work simultaneously, and results are merged.
Hierarchical: A tree of orchestrators and workers.
